consistent_cut.capture_point: The cut is established only after the authoritative composition reaches a save safe point, all save-sensitive mutation domains are quiesced, all blockers report safe, and a nonzero SaveGenerationId is allocated. Plane capture begins only after that point.
consistent_cut.mutation_rule: While the outer generation lease is held, authoritative semantic mutation and save-sensitive runtime publication are prohibited. Diagnostics and explicitly non-semantic observation may continue. No new external semantic work may be accepted into the captured generation after the cut.
consistent_cut.accepted_work_rule: External work accepted before the cut must already be represented by an authoritative durable pending/checkpoint record. If an accepted side effect exists only in transient Runtime state, capture is rejected until it is durably classified or resolved.
consistent_cut.runtime_time_rule: Runtime TimeCheckpoint is captured after the cut and before release of the same outer generation lease. Fractional remainder and immutable clock configuration identity are part of the Runtime plane payload.
consistent_cut.framework_time_rule: GameplayTimeService is captured by its reviewed Framework participant while the same outer generation lease is held. RuntimeTimeAdapter synchronization is not allowed to advance either clock during capture.
consistent_cut.runtime_persistence_rule: Only the committed Runtime Persistence snapshot/revision belongs to the generation. Transaction commit and other persistence mutation are quiesced for capture. Uncommitted transaction-local staging is outside the generation.
consistent_cut.framework_participant_rule: All 47 reviewed Framework participants are captured through SaveGameOrchestrator while the same outer generation lease is held. Generation identity belongs to the whole-generation envelope, not to each participant payload, unless future participant semantics prove a per-participant generation field necessary.
consistent_cut.release_rule: The lease is released after capture/encoding/publication succeeds or after failure cleanup has established that no new generation became authoritative.

generation_identity.name: SaveGenerationId
generation_identity.allocation_rule: First generation is 1. A subsequent generation is checked(active_generation + 1). Overflow is a hard save failure. If an existing lineage cannot be read/validated, generation allocation does not reset silently.
generation_identity.restore_validation: Reject zero, malformed, or internally inconsistent generation identity. Every plane descriptor in one envelope is bound to the envelope generation and validated before restore.

publication.rationale: Publishing Framework, Runtime Time, and Runtime Persistence as independently replaced files can expose a half-generation after interruption. The whole-engine save therefore publishes one outer package containing the already-qualified plane payloads and one generation identity.
publication.framework_payload: Canonical SaveGameImage wire produced by existing SaveGame codec.
publication.runtime_time_payload: Opaque, bounded Runtime Time v1 package bytes produced by Runtime-side composition through an injected coordination port.
publication.runtime_persistence_payload: Opaque, bounded Runtime Persistence v1 package bytes produced by Runtime-side composition through an injected coordination port.
publication.commit_boundary: Integration-owned generation store delegates one bounded byte package to the existing Base Platform atomic file replacement primitive.
publication.failed_publish_rule: A failed capture, encode, or atomic replacement never changes the previously authoritative generation.
publication.standalone_runtime_packages: The M5.2 Runtime Time and Runtime Persistence file packages remain qualified standalone durable boundaries. Whole-engine save embeds their canonical payload representation rather than publishing three independent current-generation files.

activities.scope: All state classified as PERSISTENT_OWNER/PERSISTENT_CHECKPOINT plus mutations that can change their next semantic result.
activities.cut_rule: No authoritative mutation may execute while the outer generation lease is held.
activities.resume_rule: Resume only after publication/failure cleanup releases the lease.

activities.scope: External/provider/backend work whose acceptance can outlive the initiating call.
activities.cut_rule: Acceptance before the cut must already have a durable checkpoint/outbox/reservation/reconciliation record. Transient-only accepted work is a save blocker.
activities.resume_rule: After restore, 5.4 reconciliation owns exactly-once continuation.

activities.scope: Semantic pending delivery/outbox/checkpoint queues covered by reviewed Framework participants.
activities.cut_rule: Pending semantic work is captured as data, not drained merely to permit save. Runtime-only operational queues are handled by their specific Streaming/RuntimeBridge blocker rules.
activities.resume_rule: Restore preserves durable queue identity/order according to owner contracts.

activities.scope: Deferred semantic work such as deferred-effect reconciliation and accepted integration work.
activities.cut_rule: Semantic deferred work must have a durable record before the cut. Pure budget progress with no accepted semantic side effect is outside persistence and is rebuilt/re-run.
activities.resume_rule: Durable deferred work retries from its checkpoint; non-semantic budget work restarts.

activities.scope: InMemoryPersistenceStore committed state and transaction commit boundary.
activities.cut_rule: Capture reads one committed revision. Transaction commit/mutation cannot race the snapshot. Uncommitted transaction-local staging is excluded from the generation.
activities.resume_rule: New transactions start from the restored committed revision.
Restore uses the complete TimeCheckpoint including fractional remainder.

activities.scope: GameplayTimeService clocks, schedules, trigger state and synchronization revision.
activities.cut_rule: Gameplay clock/scheduler mutation and RuntimeTimeAdapter synchronization cannot run during capture.
activities.resume_rule: Framework Time participant restores before post-restore synchronization/resume.

activities.scope: Runtime Streaming transient request execution, especially accepted external step/commit suffix state that is not durable.
activities.cut_rule: The safe-point preflight must reject capture when Streaming owns accepted-but-not-durably-represented work or is inside a transition. When safe, Streaming is quiesced and no Streaming state is serialized.
activities.resume_rule: Streaming operational state is reconstructed from authoritative state after restore.

activities.scope: RuntimeBridge materialize/dematerialize/destroy/impulse/projection processing and transient reconciliation queues.
activities.cut_rule: The safe-point preflight rejects capture while a non-reconstructible transient projection side effect is in flight or pending. Settled bindings/handles are not serialized.
activities.resume_rule: 5.4 creates fresh Runtime representations from semantic IDs; old handles/generations are never durable identity.

activities.scope: Reviewed Integration-layer delivery, outbox, reservation, cursor and reconciliation checkpoints.
activities.cut_rule: A reconciliation obligation that can affect future semantic behavior must be inside its owner participant before the cut can include the corresponding accepted work.
activities.resume_rule: 5.4 restores the checkpoint then reconciles/retries before simulation resume.

architecture.port_contract: Semantic whole-generation capture operations returning validated opaque Runtime Time and Runtime Persistence payloads/metadata. No filesystem primitives and no Framework types are required on the Runtime implementation side.
architecture.port_implementation_placement: Top-level composition that already owns both Framework Integration and Runtime services. The Integration module remains independent of Runtime Persistence/Support headers.
